calibration.auto.help: Print the grey test without dot correction and lay it flat in even light (daylight, no shadows). Point the camera at the whole piece: Stickler measures the greys as soon as it sees them and works out this printer's dot correction. A photo taken earlier works too.

preview.density.hint: Sent to the printer like the official app does, but the D11s prints the same at every level.
preview.offset.help: Fine-tunes where the design lands on the label; the preview above doesn't move. Values are printer dots: 8 dots = 1 mm, 1 dot = 0.125 mm. X is along the label: negative moves the design towards the front edge (red), positive away from it. The printer always starts about 1 mm after the front edge, so a negative X cuts off the start of the design instead of printing earlier. Y moves it across the label. "Keep label size" cuts off what moves past an edge, "Grow image" makes the printed image bigger instead.
preview.offset.calibrate_hint: To find the right offset, print the test strip from the printer sheet, under Calibration.
preview.calibration.help: Prints 3 labels, each with a different X offset, a frame on the edges and a tick every millimetre. Pick the one that sits best on its label; if none fits, tap the closest and print again. This strip:
preview.calibration.pick: Tap the one that looked best. It becomes your offset and is kept for next time:
preview.threshold.smart_hint: In Auto the threshold only applies to text, shapes and codes, which are black already, so it just makes their edges a dot thinner or bolder. Photos are dithered as they are.
preview.tone.hint: Left lighter, right darker, 128 unchanged. This mode keeps the overall grey level whatever the threshold, so the slider shifts the greys instead.

debug.intro: Transfer timing, for when prints come out wrong. The defaults work on the supported printers. Changes apply right away and are kept.
debug.chunk_delay.help: Print data goes out in small packets (200 bytes on the D11s, 180 on the MXW01) with this pause after each one. Lower is faster; too low and the printer can drop data, which shows up as shifted or missing lines. Raise it if that happens.
debug.label_pause.help: Waits between separate labels: rows of a data table and the labels of a test strip. Copies of one label go out in one job and don't use it. Try 1000 if the printer skips or garbles the labels after the first.
main.about: Label designer for the Fichero D11s and MXW01 printers
preview.grey.help: Prints 4 labels with grey patches from 10 to 100%, one for each dither mode (Atkinson at 128, as Auto uses for photos). Thermal dots spread, so greys print darker than on screen; a photo of the print in even light shows by how much.
preview.grey.help.strip: Prints one piece with a row of grey patches from 10 to 100% for each dither mode (Atkinson at 128, as Auto uses for photos). Thermal dots spread, so greys print darker than on screen; a photo of the print in even light shows by how much.
preview.grey.no_model: This printer has no dot correction yet, so the test prints without it. A photo of the print in even daylight is what a correction gets fitted from.
about.title: About & licences
about.credit.fichero: Reverse engineered the D11s protocol and wrote the Python tool and the first web version this app is built on.
about.credit.niimblue: The label designer this app grew from.
about.credit.mxw01: Documented the MXW01 printer's protocol, which the MXW01 support follows. Our own implementation.
about.credit.canvasdither: The threshold and Atkinson dithering code.
about.credit.werness: The idea behind the Werness dither mode: Brent Werness's method, as Lucas Pope described it for Return of the Obra Dinn. Our own implementation.
about.license.app: This app is free software under the GNU GPL, version 3 or later. Parts that come from other projects keep their MIT licence; their notices are in NOTICE.
about.components.help: Libraries, fonts and icons that ship in this app. Tap one to read its licence.
about.android.help: Built into the Android app. Apache-2.0 is the same licence text as material-icons above.
preview.view.bitmap.hint: Exactly what's sent to the printer, offset included.
preview.view.paper.hint: How the dots should come out when burned. A model fitted to test prints from this printer, so a guide, not exact.
preview.dotgain.hint: Thermal dots spread into each other and single dots come out faint, so greys print with more contrast than on screen. This adjusts the greys before dithering so they print closer to the design.
